owned_question: Can the exact proposed requirement set form one coherent package family for the target's documented Python-3.10.14/CUDA-12.4 context?

state_before_selection.reason: Admission had strong family-alignment evidence but had not yet bound the official Linux release build contract that constructs and verifies TorchVision's pinned Torch dependency.

new_discriminating_static_evidence: TorchVision v0.21.0 setup.py constructs an exact torch==PYTORCH_VERSION dependency when PYTORCH_VERSION is provided.
TorchVision v0.21.0 Linux wheel workflow delegates to pytorch/test-infra release/2.6.

The release/2.6 Linux build workflow exports the installed Torch release version into PYTORCH_VERSION before building and smoke-checks that the produced wheel contains a pinned Requires-Dist: torch (==...) dependency.
BiomedParse PR head independently requires torch==2.8.0 while retaining torchvision==0.21.0+cu124.

state_after_static_evidence.reason: The retained TorchVision 0.21 release contract pins Torch to the 2.6 release family, which has no version satisfying the independent direct torch==2.8.0 requirement.

candidate_investigations.why_considered: Would directly expose the exact built-wheel Requires-Dist line for the target-relevant CPython-3.10/Linux/CUDA-12.4 artifact.
candidate_investigations.why_not_needed_now: Official release build source and smoke-test contract already establish that the wheel is built with a pinned Torch 2.6-family dependency. Reading the final wheel bytes would corroborate rather than change the owned proposition state.
candidate_investigations.reactivation_trigger: Use if a future audit specifically requires byte-level artifact provenance or if authoritative build-source evidence is contradicted.

possible_observations.resolution_fails_on_torch_constraint: Would corroborate the already-established deterministic contradiction.
possible_observations.resolution_unexpectedly_succeeds: Would create a material conflict requiring diagnosis of index/artifact/specifier assumptions.
possible_observations.source_or_index_unavailable: Would be an acquisition failure, not evidence that the package set is coherent.

candidate_investigations.why_not_needed_now: The owned proposition is already resolved by authoritative static evidence plus deterministic constraint intersection. Expected failure would not improve the bounded conclusion enough to justify execution cost/acquisition variability.
TorchVision alone creates a sufficient contradiction. A second family member is unnecessary to refute package-set coherence.

candidate_investigations.why_rejected: Runtime behavior is downstream of package-family formation and would broaden into untrusted target/model execution. It cannot repair or answer the already-established package-resolution contradiction.
Mechanism-specific runtime questions may matter only after a coherent 2.8-family proposal exists. The current proposal already fails earlier.

stopping_basis: An authoritative upstream release build contract establishes the conflicting TorchVision-to-Torch family dependency.
Deterministic constraint intersection refutes coherent package-family formation.
Additional resolver/metadata observations would be corroborative unless contradictory.
Runtime/API investigation is downstream and currently pruned.
claim_limits: Does not claim global BiomedParse incompatibility with a correctly coordinated PyTorch 2.8 family.
Does not claim GPU/model runtime failure.
Does not claim safety or maintainer action.
Does not claim every PyTorch platform/index combination behaves identically.
conversation_c_learning: A candidate investigation may become unnecessary when a cheaper authoritative observation closes the proposition before execution.
Investigation selection is sequential: new evidence can prune checks that looked useful at admission time.
One decisive necessary-proposition contradiction can make additional family-member evidence redundant.
A no-further-check result is a positive technical result, not lack of analysis.
